purpose: Cases both graders must agree on. Beacon decides who is more often correct; verity decides what correct means. If the two disagree on the same answer, neither number can be cited. Cases below are of three kinds: real disagreements between the two graders, bounds one of them had wrong, and agreement baselines that must not regress. v2 (2026-08-04): the default relative bound widens to 1e-5 -- measured on beacon's answer-authority corpus, engine float-representation noise sits below it and every genuinely different number sits above 1e-4 -- and the type-discipline cases pin that NULL, booleans and numeric strings never coerce. Cross-engine canonicalization (dates to ISO, stripping) is beacon's ingestion pipeline, pinned in beacon's own suite: verity grades same-engine values and must not inherit it.

cases.why: identical values match under any tolerance
float32 representation of a float64 gold; relative difference 5e-9. Beacon called 45 of these wrong before it had a relative bound
REAL accumulated over a large aggregate; relative difference 1.8e-5. Real precision loss, not representation noise, so it fails unless a reviewer widens the tolerance for this question
relative difference 1.5e-3; a different answer

a relative bound on a large integer admits being off by one, and a count, a year or an id is either right or wrong. Whole numbers compare exactly. This case caught the defect in beacon's relative bound the day it was added
exact whole numbers still match
near zero the relative bound is vanishingly tight, so the absolute one has to carry
identical text
84 of beacon's value mismatches were this: not a tolerance question at all
identical tables
a number does not stop being a number because it sits in a table. Verity compared table cells byte-exactly, so one curated tolerance meant two different things
right rows, wrong shape. Exact-match semantics reject it; the tolerant metric is reported separately, not by loosening this
a truncated result is not the answer
row order carries meaning unless the question says otherwise
with the curated opinion, order stops carrying meaning
unordered matching has to pair rows, not sort their text: two rows equal within tolerance never sort adjacently
relative difference 9e-6, inside the v2 default of 1e-5: engine float-path noise (0.8 spelled 0.8000030517578125 by another engine), not a different answer
relative difference 2e-4, an order of magnitude above the widened bound; every genuinely different number in the measured corpus sits above 1e-4
the whole-number rule holds inside tables too: a count off by one is wrong at any tolerance
NULL is the absence of an answer, not the number zero
NULL is not the empty string either
both graders agree the answer is empty
true is a truth value, not the integer 1; a grader that coerces would score a boolean column against a count
a number rendered as text is a type error in the answer, not a tolerance question
